deckTitle: Pattern A — High-Density Pooled Multi-Tenant Architecture on Google Cloud (Workstream 2)
deckSubtitle: Serving hundreds of commercial B2B SaaS tenants on a single shared Cloud Run v2, Vertex AI Agent Engine, and AlloyDB RLS footprint with 84.7% lower inference cost and 10/10 red-team attacks blocked
tldr: Solving the Commercial SaaS Margin Equation: Pattern A hosts hundreds of Standard Tier–Enterprise Tier commercial tenants inside one shared Google Cloud project (`ramp-portal-dev`) at a 120 RPM Pooled infrastructure floor.
Cryptographic Logical Isolation (Zero Physical Sprawl): Instead of spinning up separate VPCs per tenant, Pattern A enforces non-bypassable tenant boundaries across all 5 runtime hops in software.

10/10 Adversarial Red-Team Attacks Neutralized: Competing tenants FinVault Bank and RetailStream Corp share the exact same Cloud Run v2 workers and AlloyDB cluster with zero cross-tenant data or tool bleed.

84.7% Net Inference Cost Reduction: A 32,000-token immutable platform runbook is cached once in Gemini 2.5 Pro ContextCacheConfig at a 90% discount, cutting billable input tokens from 34,000 to 5,200 per turn.

Turnkey Milestone 1 Production Kit: Includes the 80% reusable ADK 2.0 runtime pipeline, a 1-click Terraform starter (`2.6-terraform-starter`), a 90-minute hands-on codelab, and the 10-point breach simulation suite.

sections.heading: Design alternatives — Pattern A Pooled Architecture vs. Naive Multi-Tenancy vs. Dedicated Silos
tableRows: Ingress & identity binding
Trusts client-supplied `X-Tenant-Id` HTTP header or shared API key in application code
Cloud Armor strips `X-Tenant-Id`; IAP + STS mints RFC 8693 OBO & RFC 9449 DPoP context
BeyondCorp mTLS cert pinning + per-project IAM Principal Access Boundary (PAB)
Tool catalog & memory state
Global MCP tool list & shared vector collection accessible to any prompt
Hop 2 ARD visibility filter (`HTTP 403`) + `mem://{tenant_id}/L1..L5` namespace isolation
Physical per-project Agent Engine Registry & CMEK-encrypted Memory Bank
Rate limits & reasoning quotas
Regional Vertex AI RPM/TPM shared first-come, first-served (noisy-neighbor outages)
Memorystore for Valkey RPM buckets (`120`/`600` RPM, `HTTP 429`) + `4k`/`8k` thinking clamps
Dedicated GCP project quota & dedicated Provisioned Throughput / GKE GPUs
Prompt caching & FinOps COGS
34k prompt billed in full every turn (`32k Uncached/turn`) or unsafe cross-tenant cache bleed
32k immutable prefix in Gemini 2.5 Pro `ContextCacheConfig` (`90%` discount -> `84.7%` savings)
Per-silo prefix cache or dedicated air-gapped GKE Gemma 3 (27B) node pool
Relational data & PII guardrails
Application-layer `WHERE tenant_id = ?` query (vulnerable to SQLi & prompt injection)
AlloyDB `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` (`SET LOCAL`) + Model Armor (`400`/`422`) & Cloud DLP
Dedicated CMEK AlloyDB instance + `<60s` `HTTP 423 Locked` customer key kill-switch
Unit economics & target tier
High breach risk • Fails enterprise CISO security & compliance review
`120 RPM Pool / tenant / month` • High-volume commercial B2B SaaS (`10/10` breach tests PASS)
`600 RPM Silo / tenant / month` • Regulated Banking, Healthcare & Public Sector (`6/6` PASS)

sections.heading: Design considerations — The 5-Hop Cryptographic Chain in Pattern A

pipelineSteps.title: Perimeter WAF, Federated OIDC & DPoP Token Binding
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Strips unauthenticated X-Tenant-Id headers at the L7 load balancer, verifies Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra ID OIDC JWTs, and exchanges credentials via RFC 8693 OBO.
pipelineSteps.invariant: Cryptographic Claim: tenant_id + tier + DPoP (RFC 9449 jkt)
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 401 on Spoofed Header or Replayed Bearer Token

pipelineSteps.title: Tenant-Scoped Agent & MCP Tool Catalog Filtering
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Evaluates the signed TenantSecurityContext against Agent Engine Registry metadata before LLM tool-binding, returning only shared platform tools and tenant-owned private agents.
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 403 Forbidden on Cross-Tenant Agent or MCP Discovery

pipelineSteps.title: Sandboxed ADK 2.0 Execution, L1–L5 Memory & Quota Bulkheads
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Executes agent reasoning inside gVisor-isolated Cloud Run v2 / Agent Engine sandboxes, partitions L1–L5 Memory Bank namespaces, and enforces per-tenant RPM and thinking budgets.
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 429 on RPM Burst • HTTP 403 on Cross-Namespace Read

pipelineSteps.title: Bidirectional Model Armor Screening & Sensitive Data Redaction
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Screens ingress prompts and retrieved RAG chunks for prompt injection/jailbreaks, enforces tenant Natural Language Constraints (NLCs), and redacts egress PII/PCI/IBAN tokens.
pipelineSteps.invariant: Policy: inspectContent + deidentifyContent + Tenant NLC Rules
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 400 on Prompt Injection • HTTP 422 on NLC Policy Breach

pipelineSteps.title: Transactional Row-Level Security, CMEK & Zero-PII Telemetry
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Binds parameterized PostgreSQL session context (app.current_tenant_id) for mandatory Row-Level Security, verifies Cloud KMS CMEK liveness, and streams zero-PII OTel spans to BigQuery.
pipelineSteps.invariant: SQL: SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id • OTel Chargeback Ledger
pipelineSteps.gate: 0 Unauthorized Rows • HTTP 423 Locked on CMEK Revocation

bullets: Hop 1 — Edge Header Stripping & OBO/DPoP Minting: Cloud Armor strips client X-Tenant-Id headers and IAP/STS mints a DPoP-bound TenantSecurityContext.
Hop 2 — Agent Registry Discovery (ARD) Filter: Filters visible agents and MCP servers by tenant_id, blocking unauthorized private agent invocations with HTTP 403.
Hop 3 — L1–L5 Memory Bank & Valkey Bulkheads: Scopes episodic memory to mem://{tenant_id}/L1..L5, enforces 120/600 RPM in Valkey, and clamps thinking_budget (4k/8k).
Hop 4 — Bidirectional Model Armor & Sensitive Data Protection: Screens prompts for jailbreaks (HTTP 400), enforces semantic NLCs (HTTP 422), and masks egress IBAN/SWIFT/PAN PII.
Hop 5 — AlloyDB Row-Level Security & BigQuery OTel: Binds SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id in PostgreSQL RLS and streams zero-PII token attribution spans to BigQuery.

diagrams.title: Pattern A: High-Density Pooled Multi-Tenant Architecture & 5-Hop Runtime Governance
talkingPoints: Competing tenants FinVault Bank and RetailStream Corp enter the shared GCP project (ramp-portal-dev) through a single External Application Load Balancer.
Zone 1 (Hops 1 & 2): Cloud Armor strips spoofed headers, IAP + STS mints DPoP-bound OBO tokens, and Agent Engine Registry filters visible tools.
Zone 2 (FinOps & Governance): Gemini 2.5 Pro ContextCacheConfig delivers a 90% shared prefix discount while Memorystore Valkey enforces per-tenant RPM.
Zone 3 (FinVault Enterprise Slice): Runs with an 8,000-token thinking budget, OCC NLC rules, IBAN/SWIFT DLP redaction, and Google Workspace/Jira 3LO.
Zone 4 (RetailStream Standard Slice): Runs with a 4,000-token thinking cap, PCI-DSS PAN redaction, Entra ID/ServiceNow 3LO, and AlloyDB RLS.

diagrams.title: Pattern A: 10-Point Cross-Tenant Breach Simulation & Cryptographic Defense Matrix
talkingPoints: Maps all 10 automated red-team adversarial tests directly onto the 4 Hub-and-Spoke architecture zones to prove defense-in-depth.
Zone 1 Edge & Catalog Defenses (Tests 1–3): Neutralizes X-Tenant-Id header spoofing (401), private Agent Alpha probing (403), and cross-tenant MCP calls (403).
Zone 2 Rate & Consent Governance (Tests 6 & 10): Clamps oversized thinking budgets, throttles 500-RPM bursts (429), and enforces 3LO step-up consent (401).
Zone 3 Safety & DLP Defenses (Tests 4, 5 & 8): Blocks prompt injection (400), enforces OCC semantic NLCs (422), and masks egress IBAN/SWIFT/PAN PII.
Zone 4 Memory & RLS Defenses (Tests 7 & 9): Blocks cross-tenant L4 Memory Bank reads (PermissionError) and restricts AlloyDB queries to 0 unauthorized rows.

diagrams.title: Pattern A Demo Environment & Multi-IdP 2LO/3LO Auth Sandbox Topology
talkingPoints: Demonstrates how a single pooled Google Cloud project federates both Google Workspace OIDC and Microsoft Entra ID OIDC without shadow accounts.
Zone 1 (Identity Ingress): Cloud Armor WAF and IAP validate external OIDC JWTs and exchange them via IAM STS for DPoP-bound session tokens.
Zone 3 (FinVault 3LO Sandbox): Brokers Google OAuth 2.0 3LO access to Google Drive runbooks, Calendar, Gmail, and Atlassian Jira.
Zone 4 (RetailStream 3LO Sandbox): Brokers Microsoft Entra ID OIDC 3LO access to SharePoint Online and ServiceNow ITOM with step-up elicitation.
Zone 2 (Shared State & Rate Store): Firestore stores per-tenant tier metadata (8k vs. 4k budget) while Memorystore for Valkey tracks live RPM counters.

diagrams.title: Pattern A 1-Click Terraform Starter: WAF → Cloud Run v2 → Valkey / CMEK → BigQuery OTel
talkingPoints: Illustrates the declarative Terraform resource dependency graph (`2.6-terraform-starter/main.tf`) that provisions Pattern A from 5 input variables.
Zone 1 (Edge Security): Provisions `google_compute_security_policy` (Cloud Armor WAF) to block SQLi/XSS and strip unverified tenant headers.
Zone 3 (Serverless Agent Compute): Deploys `google_cloud_run_v2_service` (ADK 2.0 gateway) bound to least-privilege IAM and KMS encryption.
Zone 4 (Quota & Transactional State): Provisions `google_memorystore_instance` (Valkey HA) and AlloyDB with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.
Zone 2 (CMEK & FinOps Ledger): Creates `google_kms_crypto_key` (90-day rotation) and `google_bigquery_table` (time-partitioned OTel chargeback sink).

takeaways: High-Density Multi-Tenancy Without Compromising Security: Hundreds of commercial tenants can safely share one Cloud Run and AlloyDB footprint when cryptographic tenant context is verified across all 5 hops.

Capture 84.7% Net Inference Savings via Immutable Prefix Caching: Cache shared platform instructions once in Gemini 2.5 Pro ContextCacheConfig (90% discount) while isolating tenant memory in L1–L5 namespaces.
Eliminate Noisy Neighbors with Dual Quota Bulkheads: Pair Memorystore for Valkey token-bucket rate limiters (120 vs. 600 RPM) with per-tier Gemini thinking_budget clamps (4,000 vs. 8,000 tokens).
Prove Isolation Continuously with the 10-Point Breach Suite: Run `run_breach_simulations.py` in CI/CD to verify deterministic HTTP 400/401/403/422/429 enforcement and zero cross-tenant SQL rows.
Graduate Regulated Tenants to Pattern B/C Without Code Rewrites: Keep commercial tenants on Pattern A for maximum gross margin and promote regulated enterprises to dedicated silos via configuration.

slideSpeakerNotes.fullText:
Welcome everyone. Whether you are looking at this platform from an executive business perspective, a product strategy lens, or hands-on cloud architecture, we have structured this twelve-slide briefing into three clear acts so you always know where we are in the story.

In this session on Workstream 2, we are diving into Pattern A—our High-Density Shared Pool architecture—to show how a SaaS provider can host hundreds of commercial customers on a single shared Google Cloud stack while keeping every customer’s data, tools, and performance strictly isolated.

With that three-act roadmap in mind, let's turn to Slide 2 to meet the actual customer profiles whose business and regulatory requirements drive every design decision in this architecture.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Act I — Customer Use Cases, Competing Tenant Profiles & Cloud Stack
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Following our opening roadmap on Slide 1, we always start with the customer first—because an architecture only creates business value when it solves real customer constraints.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: Look at the business challenge on this slide: FinVault Bank and RetailStream Corp are both using our shared Incident Diagnostic Agent at the exact same time. From a financial perspective, running one shared agent runtime and sharing a single thirty-two-thousand-token system prompt cache reduces our inference cost of goods sold by up to ninety percent. At the same time, FinVault uses Google Workspace and Jira with an eight-thousand thinking-token budget, while RetailStream uses Microsoft Entra and ServiceNow with a four-thousand token cap—and neither company can ever discover or query the other’s private tools or incident history.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Act II (Level 3 Zoom) — 5-Actor Chronological Request Lifeline
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: Taking the physical components we just saw on Slide 5, this slide brings the architecture to life by tracing a single customer turn in chronological order.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatIsHappening: Tracing a single pooled request chronologically from left to right, watch how fast and disciplined the handoffs are across our five system actors. When a user sends a prompt, Hop 1 exchanges their login token for a DPoP-bound tenant context; Hop 2 filters the agent registry so private agents belonging to other customers remain invisible; Hop 3 checks the customer’s Valkey rate bucket and attaches their private memory namespace; Hop 4 screens the prompt through Model Armor while reusing the shared system prefix cache; and Hop 5 opens an AlloyDB transaction locked to that specific tenant ID.
slideSpeakerNotes.whatComesNext: Having watched the request move from hop to hop on Slide 6, a technical architect or security officer will naturally ask: what actually changes inside the data packet on the wire so a caller can never fake their company ID? Let's zoom all the way in on Slide 7.

Taking the physical components we just saw on Slide 5, this slide brings the architecture to life by tracing a single customer turn in chronological order.

When a user sends a prompt, Hop 1 exchanges their login token for a DPoP-bound tenant context; Hop 2 filters the agent registry so private agents belonging to other customers remain invisible; Hop 3 checks the customer’s Valkey rate bucket and attaches their private memory namespace; Hop 4 screens the prompt through Model Armor while reusing the shared system prefix cache; and Hop 5 opens an AlloyDB transaction locked to that specific tenant ID.
